title: Adaptive Starter Rail — Authoring & Contextual Onboarding Snippets
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an in-console authoring and runtime delivery mechanism ("Adaptive Starter Rail") for concise onboarding snippets, tooltips, and micro-guides that adapt to workspace signals (e.g., chosen model family, recent API usage pattern, cost tier). The feature allows non-engineering teams to author short contextual messages and templates that are delivered in empty states, first-run overlays, and the rollout/cost dashboards based on a simple targeting rule set.
background: Existing onboarding attempts are static text or one-size-fits-all checklists. We see dropoff when users' first actions don't match the generic guidance (e.g., users who immediately create embeddings vs. users who try chat). This work aims to reduce time-to-first-success by surfacing tailored micro-actions and code snippets relevant to the user's intent and cost sensitivity.
design_goals: Make it trivial for PMs/designers to author 1–3 line micro-guides and code snippets without developer support
Deliver guidance that adapts to runtime signals (model type, tokens consumed, recent API endpoints used, workspace tier)
Keep entry points unobtrusive: empty states, lightweight banners, and single-step starter cards
Measure impact with clear success metrics (activation, time-to-first-request, cost-aware conversions)
decisions: Authoring UI will be in Console > Settings > Onboarding > Starter Rails; simple WYSIWYG with optional code snippet block
Targeting rules are limited to a small set of signals (workspace tag, recent API call type, chosen model family, cost-tier) to avoid complexity
Delivery surfaces: empty canvas, API route quickstarts, rollout creation flow, cost card tooltips — not full-screen modals
Analytics hooks will send event 'starter_rail_shown' and 'starter_rail_action' with anonymized signal tags for measurement
tradeoffs: Keeping authoring simple means no full Turing-complete targeting language — limits expressiveness but speeds adoption
Contextual personalization increases relevance but adds risk around exposing workspace signals in shared previews (mitigated by anonymized previews)
Lightweight delivery surfaces avoid interruption but may be overlooked — balance with subtle frequency caps and progressive animation
acceptance_criteria: Authoring UI: non-engineer can create a starter rail entry with title, 1–3 lines of text, optional code snippet, and one or more simple targeting rules
Delivery: Starter rail displays in empty canvas and rollout creation flow when targeting rules match
Analytics: 'starter_rail_shown' and 'starter_rail_action' events are emitted and visible in Console analytics HUD
Experiment: We can A/B test starter rail vs baseline for a subset of new workspaces and record activation uplift within 14 days
